chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who pledged a pledge, then departed and could not be found; is the pledge sold? He said, 'No, until its owner comes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a pledged item if the debtor disappears?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the preservation of the debtor's equity in the pledged item (*rahn*) by prohibiting its sale upon mere disappearance, ensuring the owner retains the exclusive right to redeem it. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on protecting property rights against premature liquidation, distinguishing between possession and ownership in commercial transactions.
